StationProgress.title: StationProgress
StationProgress.description: Represents a user's progress within a specific station.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StationProgress entity.

isCompleted.description: Indicates whether the station is completed or not.

completionDate.description: The date that this station was completed

BiodiversityChallengeSubmission.title: BiodiversityChallengeSubmission
BiodiversityChallengeSubmission.description: Represents a user's submission for the Biodiversity Challenge (identifying flora/fauna).

id.description: Unique identifier for the BiodiversityChallengeSubmission entity.

submissionDate.description: Date and time of the submission.

isSuccessful.description: Indicates whether the submission was successful (all species identified correctly).

HabitatCreationSubmission.title: HabitatCreationSubmission
HabitatCreationSubmission.description: Represents a user's submission for the Habitat Creation challenge (uploading feeder/watering station photos).

id.description: Unique identifier for the HabitatCreationSubmission entity.

photo1Url.description: URL of the first photo (construction phase).

photo2Url.description: URL of the second photo (construction phase).

photo3Url.description: URL of the third photo (installation phase).

photo4Url.description: URL of the fourth photo (installation phase).

submissionDate.description: Date and time of the submission.

SustainabilityPractice.title: SustainabilityPractice
SustainabilityPractice.description: Represents a daily sustainable practice documented by the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SustainabilityPractice entity.

dayNumber.description: The day number of the sustainability practice (1-7).

photoUrl.description: URL of the photo documenting the sustainable practice.

practiceDescription.description: A description of the sustainable practice.

dateRecorded.description: Date when the practice was recorded.

ContentSubmission.title: ContentSubmission
ContentSubmission.description: Represents user-generated content submissions (videos, photos) for various challenges.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ContentSubmission entity.

contentUrl.description: URL of the submitted content (video link, photo URL).

submissionDate.description: Date and time of the submission.

QuizResult.title: QuizResult
QuizResult.description: Represents the result of a quiz taken by the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the QuizResult entity.

score.description: The user's score on the quiz.

completionDate.description: Date and time the quiz was completed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CrosswordPuzzle entity.

gridData.description: Stringified representation of the generated crossword puzzle grid.

clues.description: Stringified JSON array of the crossword puzzle clues.

generationDate.description: Date when the crossword was generated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the EcoQuest Explorers application, focusing on scalability, security, and ease of querying. The structure prioritizes authorization independence by denormalizing the `userId` into all subcollections, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules. Path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/...`) is used for most data to ensure clear ownership and simplified security rules. 

The `users/{userId}` collection stores core user information. Subcollections under each user (e.g., `stationProgress`, `biodiversityChallengeSubmissions`, etc.) track their progress and submissions related to the game. This hierarchical structure enables easy querying of user-specific data.

This structure directly supports the QAPs (Rules are not Filters) principle. Since data is segregated by user ID, list operations can be performed securely without needing to filter based on user identity within the rules themselves. Each subcollection is designed to hold data with a homogeneous security posture, further simplifying security rules.

The design enforces invariants by using explicit state modeling (`isCompleted` in `StationProgress`). Timestamp fields (`registrationDate`, `submissionDate`, `completionDate`, etc.) are included for auditing and chronological ordering. Standardized naming conventions (e.g., `userId` for user references) are used throughout the structure for consistency and readability.
